Senses.Explanation: Old-woman Chan is an appraisal label for talk or handling compared in the records with an old woman's solicitous speech. Masters apply it approvingly, critically, and ironically to sayings and encounters; it is not the name of a separate lineage. Dahui Zonggao asks whether the National Teacher's three calls may be called 'speaking old-woman Chan, dragging through mud and water' (說老婆禪，拖泥帶水), and elsewhere says that if he had initially explained everything this way, the student would later have cursed him. Huang Yuangong's letter contrasts Miyun Yuanwu's 'pungent handling' (手段辛辣) with people elsewhere who speak old-woman Chan. The label is also attached to actual old-woman encounters in the Floating Cup and Mount Wutai cases. Dahui Zonggao calls a line 'old-woman Chan in the great Tang country' (大唐國裏老婆禪), and Wansong Xingxiu asks whether someone with firm heels would consent to learn old-woman Chan. The term is therefore an attested appraisal label rather than the name of a separate lineage: records apply it approvingly, critically, and ironically to different sayings and encounters.
Senses.Note: The entry retains the literal gendered image because the corpus repeatedly connects the compound with an old woman's speech and with the broader collocation 'old-woman heart' (老婆心), which occurs 706 times in 214 texts; 'old-woman heart is urgent' (老婆心切) occurs 270 times in 129. The exact definition formulas yield two occurrences of 'one who speaks old-woman Chan' (說老婆禪者) and two of 'call it old-woman Chan' (喚作老婆禪), but no stable equation that narrows the label beyond the recorded comparisons and deployments.
